Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

taxastand 2.0.0.9000

Major changes

  • New ts_optimize_ref() for repeated matching against a large reference (#44, #110). (Named ts_optimize_ref() to match the other reference helpers planned in #109.) Matching spends most of its time preparing the reference (finding the genus of every name, parsing, building match keys). Pass the result of ts_optimize_ref(reference) to ts_match_names() (as reference) or ts_resolve_names() (as ref_taxonomy) and that work is done once and reused: the genus of every name is found when the reference is prepared, and each genus is parsed and keyed the first time a query needs it. Results are identical. Against a 1.6M-name WFO reference, 100 queries take about 0.2 s and 1000 queries about 1.2 s with a prepared reference once the genera are cached, versus about 4 s and 11 s without; the first call that uses a genus pays for parsing it, as before. A prepared reference holds what it has built, so it grows with use.

  • Fuzzy matching is faster for large references, with identical results (#44). Reference names whose length differs from the query’s by more than max_dist can never be within max_dist edits, so they are no longer compared; the per-query bookkeeping of the matching stages was also made linear in the number of queries, and exact-key lookups no longer hash the whole reference.

  • Breaking: a query can now match several reference records at any stage (#105). When several reference records reduce to the same name at the exact, punctuation, basionym, in, ex, rank or spelling-variant stages (for example “Willd. ex Less.” and “Willd. ex DC.” for the query “Willd.”), ts_match_names() returned only one of them, chosen by reference order. It now returns every one, as it already did for canonical-name and fuzzy matches, so the ambiguity is visible. Queries that matched a single record are unchanged.

  • Breaking: with match_autonyms = TRUE, an autonym that matches exactly after being collapsed now has match_type autonym instead of exact (#95). For example, the query “Blechnum lunare var. lunare” matching the reference name “Blechnum lunare” was reported as exact although the two names differ. Plain species names that match exactly are still exact, and a collapsed name that matches by another route keeps that match type.

  • The collapse_infra and collapse_infra_exclude arguments of ts_match_names() and ts_resolve_names() are renamed match_autonyms and match_autonyms_exclude (#101), since they are about autonyms, the infraspecific names that repeat the specific epithet. The old names still work as aliases, so existing code is unaffected; giving both an alias and its new name with different values is an error.

  • Breaking: match type auto_cfonly is renamed auto_canon (#82). The old name could be misread as a match on the taxonomic qualifier cf.; it means a match on the canonical name (genus + specific epithet + infraspecific epithet).

  • New match type auto_orthvar (#68). Epithets that differ only by standard Latin spelling variants (sylvestris/silvestris, caerulea/coerulea; ae/oe = e, y = i, ph = f, rh = r, th = t, final ii = i) are now matched exactly after folding, before fuzzy matching, instead of being reported as fuzzy matches. Code that filters on match_type may see auto_orthvar where it saw auto_fuzzy or auto_fuzzy_canon.

  • New dist column and optional swap-aware distance (#67). ts_match_names() output has a new dist column with the edit distance of each fuzzy hit (NA for other match types; a new column, so code that selects columns by position may need updating). The new argument transpositions = TRUE counts a swap of two adjacent letters (Qurecus for Quercus) as one edit instead of two. It is off by default (plain Levenshtein distance, as before, and somewhat faster). With max_dist = 1, 188 swapped-letter PPG queries were all found with it on, versus none with it off; at the default max_dist = 3 the effect is small.

  • Breaking: fuzzy matching of queries without an author (#49). The author string used to count towards the edit distance, so author-less queries could only fuzzy-match (loosely, and only because the old default max_dist was large). They are now fuzzy-matched on the canonical name (genus + specific epithet + infraspecific epithet), ignoring the author. A canonical-name match is reported as auto_canon, and a misspelled one as the new match type auto_fuzzy_canon; all reference names within max_dist are returned, so ambiguity shows up in ts_resolve_names(). The new argument fuzzy_canon_hits = "closest" instead keeps only the nearest hits (ties kept), which avoids unrelated names with short epithets. Queries with an author are still matched on the whole name (auto_fuzzy).

  • Breaking: the default max_dist is now 3 (was 10) (#47). max_dist is the Levenshtein distance on the whole depunctuated name including the author, and 10 was very loose (for example, 5 queries against PPG returned 275 result rows). The distance is also now plain Levenshtein distance: the extra +1 penalty taxon-tools applied when the reference merely has extra trailing text was removed, which can add matches at exactly max_dist.

  • Design philosophy change: taxastand is no longer a strict port of taxon-tools. Goals are now to standardize names accurately (including authors), quickly, and flexibly (custom reference databases), rather than to implement taxon-tools in R. Output may diverge from taxon-tools in future releases. The docker differential test and the “pure R vs. taxon-tools” benchmark vignette were removed.

  • Add strip_qualifiers argument to ts_parse_names(), ts_match_names(), and ts_resolve_names(), so that open-nomenclature qualifiers (cf., aff., s.l./sensu lato, s.str./sensu stricto) can optionally be removed from names before parsing/matching, instead of being mis-captured as the specific epithet. Off by default (#40)

Performance

  • Name matching is much faster for large references (e.g. ~20 s to ~1 s for 5 queries against the 78k-name PPG taxonomy). ts_match_names() and ts_resolve_names() now ignore reference names whose genus cannot match any query genus before parsing the reference (#43); match keys are computed lazily and looked up in vectorised passes instead of per-key hash maps (#45); and tt_matchnames() returns a data frame instead of delimited strings (#46). ts_parse_names() is also about twice as fast, because the per-row failure check and tidyr::separate() were replaced with vectorised base R (#44). Results are unchanged, except that multiple fuzzy matches to one query are now returned in reference order.

Bug fixes

  • Fix ts_match_names(..., collapse_infra = TRUE)’s internal deduplication key, which used paste0(..., sep = "_") – paste0() has no sep argument, so the separator was silently dropped, joining name components with no delimiter between them. This could in rare cases cause two genuinely different names to be treated as duplicates during deduplication if their concatenated components happened to coincide. Found via static analysis while running pkgcheck::pkgcheck() ahead of rOpenSci submission.

Minor improvements

  • New ts_format_ref() turns a table of taxonomic names (for example from a downloaded taxonomic database) into a reference: it renames columns with col_map, adds scientificNameAuthorship to scientificName, drops ranks above species and tidies values (#112, part of #109).

  • New ts_subset_ref() keeps one or more taxa (for example a family) and their synonyms from a large table of names, using higher-rank columns or parentNameUsageID, so a whole database need not be made into a reference (#114, part of #109).

  • ts_format_ref() now also keeps the columns that give the hierarchy of the names (higher ranks such as family, and parentNameUsageID), so ts_subset_ref() can be used before or after it for most tables (#121, part of #109).

  • The argument that holds the reference is now called ref in ts_match_names(), ts_resolve_names(), ts_optimize_ref(), ts_format_ref() and ts_subset_ref(), so that it is the same everywhere (#120, part of #109). The old names, reference in ts_match_names() and ref_taxonomy in ts_resolve_names(), still work as aliases and will be deprecated in a future version. Only calls that name the argument are affected; its position is unchanged.

  • ts_format_ref() now gives a made-up unique taxonID to names that have none (some databases give none to synonyms), because ts_resolve_names() could not resolve those names (#117, part of #109).

  • New ts_load_ref() loads a reference, formats it with ts_format_ref(), and optionally keeps only some taxa (taxon). The data come from a named source ("wfo", the World Flora Online Plant List; "ppg", the Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group classification; or the taxadb snapshots of "itis", "col", "gbif", "ncbi", "ott", "fb" and "slb", which need the nanoparquet or the duckdb package (with duckdb, taxon is applied while reading, which is much faster for large tables like GBIF); see the new ts_show_ref_sources() for licenses and citations; with versions = TRUE it also lists the versions you can download), an HTTPS url, or a file (CSV/TSV, zipped Darwin Core Archive or Parquet). The latest version of a named source is used unless a version is given, and the version, license and citation are recorded in the ts_source attribute. Downloads are kept in a folder only if you give a cache_dir (otherwise they are in tempdir()) (#115, #116, #117, part of #109).

  • Messages are controlled by one package option, taxastand.verbosity (#133). options(taxastand.verbosity = "quiet") silences the messages and the warnings about names that were excluded (not parsed or placeholders), in ts_load_ref(), ts_show_ref_sources(), ts_show_ref_cache(), ts_clear_ref_cache(), ts_parse_names(), ts_match_names() and ts_resolve_names(); the default is "inform". This follows rOpenSci advice to set verbosity at the package level. The unreleased quiet argument of ts_load_ref() was removed. ts_parse_names(quiet = TRUE) still works but is superseded by the option. ts_load_ref() now gives one line (Loaded 309 names from ITIS (version 2026), license CC0.), no longer reports the path of a cached file, and gives the citation once per R session for each source (it is always in attr(x, "ts_source")).

  • New ts_show_ref_cache() and ts_clear_ref_cache() list and delete the files downloaded by ts_load_ref(); other files in the folder are never touched (#132, part of #109).

  • manual_match in ts_match_names() now also works when query is a dataframe of names parsed with ts_parse_names() (#93), not only a character vector. The query values are compared with the name column.

  • The documentation of ts_match_names() and ts_resolve_names() now recommends ts_optimize_ref() for repeated queries against a large reference, and ts_match_names() defines an autonym (#94).

  • New “Benchmarks” vignette comparing taxastand with similar packages (#96, #103): taxastand, taxify, WorldFlora and U.Taxonstand match the same World Flora Online reference against queries made by damaging real names (typos in the genus, epithet and author, missing authors, homonyms) and by changing the form of names in the ways taxastand checks for (a missing basionym author, a dropped ex element, a changed infraspecific rank, a Latin spelling variant), so the right answer is known. It compares accuracy, single answers and speed. The results are precomputed and saved with the package, and the code that produced them is installed in system.file("benchmark", package = "taxastand").

  • Faster fuzzy matching: candidates are looked up by reference row rather than by name (a 600-query PPG run took 2.4 s, now 2.1 s; results identical).

  • Faster parsing and key building (#66): fewer and cheaper regex passes, and pipe-delimited records are split once instead of once per field. Output is identical; e.g. parsing 149,000 names takes about 1.2 s instead of 3.2 s.

  • Lighter installation (#48): dplyr, tidyr, fs and glue are no longer dependencies (the resolve and match steps now use base R, with identical output), and tibble moved to Suggests. tbl_out = TRUE (or the ts_tbl_out option) now requires the tibble package to be installed. magrittr is also no longer a dependency, so breaking: %>% is no longer re-exported; load magrittr or dplyr, or use the native pipe |>.

  • Document the match_type values in a new “Match types” section of ?ts_match_names, grouped by how far each can be trusted (#52); the match type codes themselves are unchanged

  • Use vapply() instead of sapply(), anyDuplicated() instead of any(duplicated(x)), and drop several redundant x == TRUE/x == FALSE comparisons

  • Fix a dead link in the README (“The Plant List”, no longer online; now links to a Wayback Machine snapshot)

  • New vignette “Using taxadb” shows how to get a reference from a standard taxonomic database (ITIS, with a note on others) with the taxadb package and match against it (#107).

taxastand 2.0.0

Major changes

  • Implement pure R solution for name parsing and matching
  • Add manual_match argument to ts_match_names(), so users can supply a dataframe of manually matched names that override the matching algorithm (#4)

taxastand 1.0.0

Major changes

  • Add Docker support for running taxon-tools, so it no longer needs to be installed locally
  • Add collapse_infra and collapse_infra_exclude arguments to ts_match_names() and ts_resolve_names(), for collapsing infraspecific taxa to their species when matching
  • Add quiet argument to ts_parse_names() to suppress warnings

Bug fixes

  • Fix mapping of match results after collapsing infraspecific taxa
  • Fix matched_status incorrectly showing as NA for some results
  • Replace empty strings with NA in results

taxastand 0.0.0.9000

Major changes

  • Initial implementation of ts_parse_names(), ts_match_names(), and ts_resolve_names(), using the external taxon-tools system dependency for parsing and fuzzy matching
  • Add package website via pkgdown and an introductory vignette
